overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that typing a drive letter followed by a colon and backslash (e.g., "Q:\") would be handled the same way as typing a POSIX root path with a trailing separator, but it failed to account for Windows drive root paths having no trailing separator and a different path parsing behavior.
why_it_breaks: The code added a check `!resources.hasTrailingPathSeparator(filePickBoxUri, this.separator)` to prevent skipping folder refresh when the entered path has a trailing separator (e.g., "/folder/"). However, on Windows, typing a drive letter like "Q:" followed character-by-character does not produce a trailing separator until the user types a backslash. The agent's fix assumed that any path with a trailing separator should skip the refresh, but it did not handle the case where the user types just the drive root (e.g., "Q:") without a separator. When the user types "Q:", the path has no trailing separator, so the condition fails, and the dialog incorrectly treats it as a different folder than the current, causing no matching entries to be shown. Pasting the full path works because it may trigger a different code path or the full string comparison handles the drive root correctly.

evidence.quote: The simple file dialog updated the path but skipped refreshing contents when navigating from `/` into a child folder.
